lessons.title: Meet your board
lessons.copy: Find the USB port, power pins, digital pins and the processor that runs your sketch.
lessons.outcome: Identify the board, ground, power and a digital pin.

quiz.question: What is GND used for in a basic circuit?
quiz.explain: Correct! GND is the circuit’s ground reference. Check wiring before powering real hardware.

lessons.title: Blink an LED
lessons.copy: Use setup, loop, pinMode, digitalWrite and delay to make a light blink.
lessons.outcome: Change the blink interval and explain HIGH versus LOW.

quiz.question: Which function runs once when a board starts?
quiz.explain: Correct! setup() runs once; loop() repeats while the board is running.

lessons.title: Read a button
lessons.copy: Turn a physical input into a program decision with a digital read.
lessons.outcome: Describe input pins, pull-up logic and a simple if statement.

quiz.question: With INPUT_PULLUP, a pressed button wired to GND usually reads…
quiz.explain: Correct! The internal pull-up makes the idle state HIGH; connecting the input to GND makes it LOW.

lessons.title: Read a sensor
lessons.copy: Follow a sensor signal into your program and inspect the output.
lessons.outcome: Trace a sensor reading from input to serial output.

quiz.question: Where can you inspect measurements printed by Serial.println()?
quiz.explain: Correct! Serial Monitor displays text sent over the serial connection at a matching baud rate.

lessons.title: Talk over Serial
lessons.copy: Print useful messages and measurements to make invisible code easier to debug.
lessons.outcome: Choose a baud rate and explain println versus print.

quiz.question: What does Serial.println(value) do?

answers.text: Prints a value then starts a new line
Changes a GPIO pin to HIGH

quiz.explain: Correct! println writes text and ends the line, making readings easier to scan.

lessons.title: Read analog values
lessons.copy: Turn a potentiometer or light sensor into a changing number.
lessons.outcome: Explain analogRead and why ADC ranges depend on the board.

quiz.question: Which function reads an analog input on Arduino-style boards?
quiz.explain: Correct! analogRead samples an ADC input; resolution and voltage range depend on the board.

lessons.title: Dim an LED with PWM
lessons.copy: Use pulse-width modulation to control perceived brightness.
lessons.outcome: Relate a PWM duty value to LED brightness and pin limits.

quiz.question: What does increasing PWM duty cycle usually do to an LED?
quiz.explain: Correct! A higher duty cycle keeps the output active for more of each PWM period.

lessons.title: Move a servo
lessons.copy: Command a small servo to move between safe target angles.
lessons.outcome: Explain angle commands and why servos may need separate power.

quiz.question: What is the safest assumption about a servo’s power needs?

answers.text: Check current needs; use suitable power
Any GPIO pin can power it directly

quiz.explain: Correct! Servos can draw more current than a GPIO can supply. Use a suitable supply and common ground.

lessons.title: Measure distance
lessons.copy: Understand ultrasonic trigger and echo timing for obstacle sensing.
lessons.outcome: Describe how echo travel time becomes an estimated distance.

quiz.question: An ultrasonic sensor estimates distance mainly from…
quiz.explain: Correct! The sensor measures sound pulse travel time and converts it to an estimated distance.

lessons.title: ESP32 goes online
lessons.copy: Explore Wi-Fi capability and the extra care needed for network credentials.
lessons.outcome: Distinguish ESP32 3.3 V logic from Uno 5 V logic and keep secrets out of code shared publicly.

quiz.question: What should you remember about ESP32 GPIO logic?
quiz.explain: Correct! ESP32 GPIO is generally 3.3 V logic and is not usually 5 V tolerant.

lessons.title: Drive a DC motor
lessons.copy: Learn why a motor driver sits between a microcontroller and a motor.
lessons.outcome: Explain direction control, PWM speed control and common ground.

quiz.question: Why use a motor driver with a microcontroller?

answers.text: Motors need more current and switching protection

quiz.explain: Correct! A suitable driver handles motor current and switching; follow its wiring and protection guidance.

lessons.title: Build a mini robot
lessons.copy: Combine sensing, decisions and motor control into a simple robot plan.
lessons.outcome: Sketch a safe sense-decide-act loop for an obstacle-avoiding robot.

quiz.question: What is a basic robot control loop?
quiz.explain: Correct! A robot repeatedly senses its environment, decides what to do, and acts.
